# Main Street Growth: 30-day Instagram plan (from 2026-11-16, generated by `money_machines/content_plan.py`)

**What it is for:** Teaches local business owners the basics the agency sells (Google profile, fast phone website, honest reviews) and sends interested owners to the free website check on the agency storefront (team B3).

**Bio:** Simple, honest tips to get more local customers: Google, websites, reviews. Free website check: link below.

**Handle ideas (check they are free):** @mainstreet.growth, @localgrowth.notes, @thelocalgrowthdesk

**Rules:**

- Post from the owner's own account; schedule in Meta Business Suite (free) or ig_post.py with his own token.
- At most 5 hashtags; captions under 2200 characters; alt text on every image.
- No bought followers, likes or comments; no follow/unfollow or auto-DM tools (Instagram bans automated engagement).
- Never promise rankings; examples are labelled as examples; no fake reviews or review tricks.
- Interested owners go to the free website check (agency storefront), not to cold DMs.

## Day 1: Mon 2026-11-16 11:45

```
5 things your Google profile needs this week

Your Google Business Profile is often the first thing a new customer sees, before your website, before your Instagram. It is free, and most local businesses leave half of it empty. Fix these five this week and you are ahead of most of your street.

1. Your real business name, nothing added
2. The most specific main category
3. Correct hours, holidays too
4. 10+ real photos
5. A reply to every review

Save this for later.

#smallbusiness #localbusiness #smallbusinesstips #googlebusinessprofile #localseo
```

## Day 2: Tue 2026-11-17 11:45

```
Your website has 3 seconds

People on a phone decide fast. If they can't tell what you do, where, and how to reach you in about three seconds, they go back to Google and tap the next result. Open your own site on your phone right now and check those three things.

1. Say what you do and where, in one line
2. Phone number at the top, tap-to-call
3. One big button: Call, Book or Get a quote

Send this to a business owner who needs it.

## Day 3: Wed 2026-11-18 11:45

```
How to ask for a review without feeling awkward

Most happy customers would leave a review. They just forget, or can't find where. Ask at the right moment, make it one tap, and ask everyone the same way. Rewards for reviews break Google's rules and the FTC's review rule, so keep it simple: just ask.

1. Ask right after a good moment
2. Send the direct link, not 'search us'
3. Ask every customer, not only happy ones
4. Never offer a reward

Want to know how your website does on a phone? Free 60-second website check: link in bio.

#smallbusiness #customerreviews #localbusiness #smallbusinesstips #shoplocal
```

Alt text: Text card from Main Street Growth: How to ask for a review without feeling awkward. Ask right after a good moment; Send the direct link, not 'search us'; Ask every customer, not only happy ones; Never offer a reward.

Is your website losing calls? A 2-minute test

You don't need a tech person for this test. Do it once a month. A broken form or a number that doesn't dial loses customers silently, and you never hear about it.

## Day 9: Tue 2026-11-24 11:45

```
Why your website should load in under 3 seconds

Slow pages lose visitors, especially on a phone with a weak signal. The fix is often simple: smaller images and fewer extras. Google's free PageSpeed Insights shows what slows you down.

1. Big photos are the usual problem
2. Shrink images before you upload
3. Fewer plugins and pop-ups
4. Test free with PageSpeed Insights

Questions? Ask in the comments and I'll answer.

#smallbusiness #localbusiness #smallbusinesstips #googlebusinessprofile #localseo
```

Alt text: Text card from Main Street Growth: Why your website should load in under 3 seconds. Big photos are the usual problem; Shrink images before you upload; Fewer plugins and pop-ups; Test free with PageSpeed Insights.

## Day 10: Wed 2026-11-25 11:45

```
Don't stuff keywords into your business name

It is tempting to add keywords to your name on Google. It breaks Google's guidelines and can get your profile suspended. Your services, categories and description are where those words belong.

1. Use your real name, as on your sign
2. 'Best plumber in town' in the name can get you suspended
3. Put services in the Services section

Follow for one simple tip a day.
